subject: Post-call recap: ZenithAI TCO & cost levers (batching / caching / quantization)
summary: Post-call recap capturing ZenithAI's cost pain (token spend + latency), suggested TCO levers (batching, caching, quantization), and next steps for a pilot / detailed TCO review.
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@zenithai.com>, Priya Sharma <priya@zenithai.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: ZenithAI TCO & cost levers (batching / caching / quantization)

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned.

Pain points you shared
- Monthly inference spend is spiking and unpredictable (esp. peak periods for batch scoring).
- Latency requirements for interactive features are 150–300ms P95; current provider misses this during bursts.
- Concern about data residency and auditability for customer PII.

Goals we discussed
- Reduce unit cost per generated token while keeping P95 latency <= 300ms for UI flows.
- Put a pilot in place to validate 3 months of production traffic (~100M tokens/month).
- Evaluate Dedicated vs Private deployment for residency & compliance.

TCO levers we recommend (high level)
1) Batching: for async scoring jobs you can batch to increase GPU utilization — expect 2–4x throughput improvement for those workloads with minimal cost increase per GPU hour.
2) Prefix/KV caching: for repeated prompts (e.g., similar system prompts or reused contexts) caching reduces repeated compute; can cut token compute by up to 30% on some flows.
3) Quantization: int8/in4 model variants usually drop model inference costs by ~25–45% depending on accuracy/QA tolerance.
4) Smart routing: route low-latency interactive traffic to smaller, faster variants and background jobs to cost-optimized variants.

Rough cost framing (very high-level, see attached workbook for line-item math)
- Current spend (your estimate): ~$22k/month for current vendor at your reported 100M tokens/month.
- Redwood hosted estimate (mix of streaming + embeddings): ~$14k/month (with batching & cache assumptions in workbook).
- Dedicated reserved pool (pilot sized): one-week forecast in workbook shows potential 30–40% savings vs current vendor at steady state.

Attachments: I attached a TCO workbook (zenithai_tco_model_v1.xlsx) and our pricing sheet (redwood_pricing_sheet_v4.pdf). The workbook includes an adjustable assumptions sheet (tokens/month, batching factor, cache hit rate, quantization choices).

Next steps
- I’ll follow up with a filled-in TCO using your example traffic profile (100M tokens/mo) by EOD Monday.
- Rafael can scope the pilot (tech checklist + data residency options) and propose a timeline.
- If useful, schedule a 30-min technical deep-dive next week to validate latency SLOs.

Available times: Tue/Wed 9–11am PT.

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0198

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@zenithai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya@zenithai.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 16:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: ZenithAI TCO & cost levers (batching / caching / quantization)

Thanks Marissa — good notes. A couple of clarifying q's:
1) Do you support KV cache for long-context flows (we have >8k token histories for some agents)? How does that affect memory on the GPU (esp. for dedicated pools)?
2) Can you drop a back-of-envelope for 100M tokens/month with our current latency constraint (assume 200ms P95 target)? I want to see hosted vs dedicated delta.
3) Data residency: we need EU data to stay in EU. What are options for a pilot and for production?

Priya will coordinate schedules. Happy to do Tue 9am PT.

—Alex
Head of Product, ZenithAI
alex.johnson@zenithai.com | +1 510 555 0123

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@zenithai.com>, Priya Sharma <priya@zenithai.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 08:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: ZenithAI TCO & cost levers (batching / caching / quantization)

Hey Alex — quick answers and I've attached a baseline TCO for 100M tokens with conservative assumptions. See the "Assumptions" tab.

1) KV cache + long context:
- Yes, our runtime supports KV cache for long-context flows. For sequences >8k we keep per-request KV state on GPU memory; the main RAM/GPU impact is KV storage which scales with active concurrent sessions and average sequence length.
- For Dedicated pools we size VM/GPU memory based on peak concurrent chars; Rafael will propose recommended pool sizes in the pilot scope.

2) Back-of-envelope for 100M tokens/month (high-level):
- Current vendor (your estimate): $22,000/month.
- Redwood Hosted (mixed): ~$13,800/month (assumes batching factor 1.3 for interactive + 4.0 for async scoring; cache hit 25%; quantization to int8 for background models).
- Redwood Dedicated (small reserved pool pilot): ~$9,400/month (assumes 30% improved GPU utilization via batching + 30% cache effective reduction).
- Notes: Dedicated involves a baseline reserved cost; the per-token math is in the workbook. These are directional — Rafael will run a detailed simulation.

3) Data residency:
- Pilot: EU region hosted (we have EU hosted endpoints) or Dedicated deployed in EU region. Both options provide EU data residency.
- Production: Private deployment (VPC) is available for strict residency + KMS controls.

Next steps I propose:
- Rafael to send a pilot scope + required tech checklist (data transfer, encryption, SLA expectations).
- I’ll drop the completed 100M-token TCO in HubSpot and Drive by EOD.
- Schedule Tue 9am PT tech deep-dive (works for me).

Link to HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cZenithAI-TCO

See attached workbook for full numbers.

Best,
Marissa

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@zenithai.com>, Priya Sharma <priya@zenithai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: ZenithAI TCO & cost levers (batching / caching / quantization)

Alex / Priya —

Happy to run the detailed sim and scope the pilot. A few technical notes from my side:
- Batching tradeoffs: for interactive flows we recommend conservative batching (1.2–1.5) to avoid pushing P95 beyond 300ms. For async jobs, we can push batching much higher (3–6x) to maximize token throughput.
- Cache hit assumptions: a 25% cache hit is conservative for reuse-heavy prompts; if you have stronger repeat patterns we often see 30–40% reduction in compute.
- Quantization: int8 works well for many encoder-decoder and decoder-only variants; we’ll include a small eval set to validate quality degradation (<2% delta on key metrics).

Pilot scope (proposed)
- 4-week pilot in EU region (hosted dedicated pool)
- Goal: validate cost savings and ensure 200ms P95 for the interactive path
- Deliverables: baseline perf/cost report, pilot tuning, post-pilot TCO with measured numbers

I’ll prepare the pilot SOW and a short tech checklist (network egress, test tokens, any data sampling) and share by Monday EOD.

If Tue 9am PT works, I’ll send a calendar invite.

—Rafael
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0147
